parts: Here is the core brief for Project Alpha. We need to lock down the engineering launch for November 15, 2026. The budget cap is strictly set at $45,000.
Understood. I will log the Project Alpha engineering target for November 15, 2026, with a maximum financial ceiling of $45,000. Do we have stakeholder sign-off on this allocation?
Yes, Sarah formally approved the entire $45,000 budget yesterday afternoon. No further executive clearances are required to move forward.

Let's document our platform support obligations. Our critical system bugs (Severity 1) carry an ironclad 4-hour resolution SLA. General non-blocking maintenance updates must be handled exclusively on weekend maintenance windows (Saturday 02:00 - 06:00 UTC).
Logged: Severity 1 bugs have a 4-hour SLA. Maintenance is scheduled for Saturdays 02:00-06:00 UTC. What is the SLA for Severity 2 bugs?
Severity 2 issues have a 24-hour turnaround target, and regular feature requests are prioritized in two-week sprint cycles.

Our backend architecture must remain exclusively Python 3.11+ using FastAPI for asynchronous endpoints and PostgreSQL for persistent relational data. We do not approve introducing Redis or MongoDB unless cloud costs exceed $500/month.

For real-time audio and inference, local processing on macOS must target Apple Silicon MPS acceleration with int8 or float16 quantization to guarantee sub-1.5s latency without cloud transcription dependencies.

Standard payment terms for all corporate deliverables are Net 30 from the invoice issue date. A 5% discount applies if paid within 10 days. Late payments incur a 1.5% monthly compound fee after 45 days.
